title: One God or Many?
welcome_lead: Explore how religions answer the deepest question: how many gods are there?
meta_desc: KS3 Religious Studies adventure on monotheism and polytheism across world religions.

concepts.def: Belief in many gods or deities.

walkthroughs.body_html: Judaism, Christianity and Islam are monotheistic — they teach that there is only one God who created everything. Sikhism also teaches belief in one God, called Waheguru.

Hinduism is often described as polytheistic because Hindus worship many deities such as Brahma, Vishnu and Shiva. However, many Hindus believe these gods are all aspects of one ultimate reality called Brahman.
Buddhism is unusual — most Buddhists do not focus on a creator God. Instead they follow the teachings of the Buddha to escape suffering and reach enlightenment (Nirvana).

mcqs.q: What does the Abrahamic covenant in Judaism involve?
options: Being 'chosen' means Jews believe they are superior to other peoples.
God's promise to Abraham of land, descendants and blessing, in return for faithfulness — the foundational covenant marking Jews as a covenant people with responsibilities, not privileges.
Natural evil means evil that is good for nature.
The covenant means Jews must not interact with non-Jews.

mcqs.q: How do Muslims believe the Quran was revealed?
options: The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.
Natural evil means evil that is good for nature.
Muhammad wrote the Quran based on his own teachings.
Through the angel Jibril (Gabriel) to Muhammad over 23 years; Muslims believe it is the literal word of God, not Muhammad's own words.

mcqs.q: What distinction matters for the free will defence to the problem of evil?
options: The free will defence solves all forms of evil at once.
The Quran was written by Allah and dropped from heaven.

Between moral evil (caused by free human choices) and natural evil (earthquakes, disease) — the free will defence directly addresses moral evil but struggles with natural evil, which isn't a product of free choice.
Natural evil means evil that is good for nature.
